outputs.exact_statement: For every integer $n\geq3$ there is a unital trace-preserving normal $*$-isomorphism $$L(\mathbb F_n)\cong L(\mathbb F_{n+1}).$$
There exists a unital normal trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism $$\Phi:L(\mathbb F_2)\longrightarrow L(\mathbb F_3).$$
For a freely generating Haar $d$-tuple $U$ in $M$, the assignment $\lambda(x_j)\mapsto U_j$ extends to a unital normal trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism $L(\mathbb F_d)\to M$.
The algebras $A_gW^*(C)A_g^*$, $g\in\Gamma$, form a free family. In particular, each $S_g$ is free from the von Neumann algebra generated by all $S_b$ with $b\ne g$.
A monomial with nonidentity label has trace zero. A monomial with identity label can be expressed as a product of variables $S_g$ (or as the constant $1$).

For every such $k$, $$\label{eq:free-sum}
 \left\lVert s(k)\right\rVert\leq K\left\lVert k\right\rVert_{\ell^2},\qquad K=3\pi.$$

There is a one-parameter group $(\beta_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ of unital trace-preserving normal $*$-automorphisms of $M$ that fixes $S$ and whose restriction to $$B=C^*(A_1,\ldots,A_n,S)$$ is point-norm continuous. Writing $A_j(t)=\beta_t(A_j)$ and evaluating group words at this tuple, the paths satisfy $$\frac{d}{dt}A_j(t)=\mathrm is_t(h_j)A_j(t),\qquad s_t(k)=\sum_{g\in\Gamma}k(g)A_g(t)SA_g(t)^*,\qquad A_j(0)=A_j. \label{eq:flow-ode}$$ The derivatives here are in operator norm. With $K=3\pi$ as in [eq:free-sum], for every $t\in\mathbb R$, $$\begin{aligned} \left\lVert \beta_t(A_j)-A_j\right\rVert &\leq |t|K\|h_j\|_{\ell^2}, \label{eq:generator-displacement}\\ \left\lVert \beta_t(A_w)-\exp(\mathrm itS)A_w\right\rVert &\leq |t|K\|D_w-\delta_e\|_{\ell^2} \qquad(w\in\Gamma). \label{eq:word-displacement} \end{aligned}$$ In particular, at $t=1$ the target in [eq:word-displacement] is $CA_w$.

For every $p\in\mathcal P$ and every integer $r\geq1$, $$\tau\bigl(\operatorname{ev}_0(\delta^r p)\bigr)=0.
 \label{eq:universal-trace-identity}$$

Let $E$ be any closed unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $M$ containing $S$, and let $V_1,\ldots,V_n$ be unitaries in $E$. The equation $X'=\mathcal V(X)$ with $X(0)=V$ has a unique global solution in $E^n$ that is smooth in norm, and all its coordinates remain unitary.

Let $n\geq 3$ and $\eta>0$. There exist a word $w\in\Gamma$ and a finitely supported real coefficient vector $h$ such that the cocycle determined by $$h_1=h,\qquad h_j=0\quad(2\leq j\leq n)$$ satisfies $$\label{eq:small-cocycle}
  \|h\|_{\ell^2}<\eta,
  \qquad
  \|D_w-\delta_e\|_{\ell^2}<\eta.$$

For each $m\geq 1$, the elements $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ freely generate a free subgroup of $\Gamma$. If $h_1=h$ and $h_j=0$ for $j\geq 2$, then $$\label{eq:cocycle-word-value}
  D_{w_m}=T_m h.$$

Let $n\geq 3$, and let $(A_1,\ldots,A_n,C)$ be a freely generating Haar tuple in a finite von Neumann algebra $(M,\tau)$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are a trace-preserving normal automorphism $\alpha$ of $M$ and a word $w\in\mathbb F_n$ such that, with $A_j'=\alpha(A_j)$, $$\label{eq:perturbation}
 \max_{1\leq j\leq n}\left\lVert A_j'-A_j\right\rVert<\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \left\lVert A_w'-C\right\rVert<\varepsilon.$$ The tuple $(A_1',\ldots,A_n',C')$, where $C'=\alpha(C)$, is again freely generating Haar. Here the target in the second estimate is the original $C$; the new completion is $$C'=C A_w^*,$$ where $A_w$ is evaluated on the original $n$-tuple.

For all $1<r,s\leq\infty$ there is a unital normal trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism $L(\mathbb F_r)\cong L(\mathbb F_s)$. Moreover, $$\mathcal F\bigl(L(\mathbb F_r)\bigr)=\mathbb R_{>0}
 \qquad(1<r\leq\infty).$$

Let $M=L(\mathbb F_2)$ with its canonical trace. For every integer $n\geq2$ there are a self-adjoint $n$-tuple $X^{(n)}$ and a self-adjoint $2n$-tuple $Y^{(n)}$ such that $$W^*(X^{(n)})=W^*(Y^{(n)})=M$$ and $$\delta(X^{(n)})=\delta_0(X^{(n)})=n,
 \qquad
 \delta^*(Y^{(n)})=\delta^\star(Y^{(n)})=n.$$ Consequently, none of $\delta,\delta_0,\delta^*,\delta^\star$ is invariant under changing a finite self-adjoint $W^*$-generating tuple of a tracial von Neumann algebra. Each takes unbounded values on such generating tuples of the single factor $L(\mathbb F_2)$.
